takeaways: At 320 CSS px wide, content fits without scrolling in two directions. That equals a 1280px-wide window zoomed to 400%.
For content that scrolls sideways, such as vertical text, the test is 256 CSS px tall.
No content or function is lost. The narrow layout can stack columns, collapse navigation into a menu and wrap text.
Exception: parts that need a two-dimensional layout, such as maps, data tables, diagrams, video and editors whose toolbars must stay in view. They may scroll; the rest of the page still reflows.
failures: A fixed-width layout that scrolls sideways at 400% zoom
Sticky headers and footers that fill the screen when zoomed
Content hidden in the mobile layout with no way to reach it
check: Set a frame to 320px wide and lay out every key screen in it.
In the build, set the window to 1280px and zoom to 400%. Read the page scrolling only down.
Check that nothing is cut off, overlapping or missing compared with the wide view.

quiz.question: At 320px a data table is wider than the screen. Everything else on the page fits. Does the page pass?
options: Only if the table turns into cards
Yes. The table may scroll sideways on its own
quiz.why: A data table needs rows and columns to make sense, so it is exempt. The rest of the page must reflow, so give the table its own scroll area.

spec: Provide a 320px-wide layout for each template, and say what changes.
Mark which regions may scroll in two directions, and why.
Say how sticky elements behave when space is tight, such as becoming static.
review: What does this look like at 400% zoom?
Which parts truly need two-dimensional scrolling?
How much of the screen is left once sticky bars are shown?
tradeoff: Hiding things on small screens keeps them tidy, but anything hidden must still be reachable. Collapse into menus and disclosures rather than removing content. Text size alone is 1.4.4.
system: Make every component responsive down to 320px, and give tables and media a built-in scroll container.
pitch: Zooming in is how many people with low vision read. If they have to scroll sideways on every line, they give up.
